PullRequest.Title: sessions: Show catalog chats in the session list
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Show the default chat and lightweight peer-chat metadata from the Agent Host session catalog directly in the Agents Window session list.

- preserve the catalog's ordered chat identities, titles, origins, and interactivity without loading transcripts
- keep peer-chat facades stable while live session state enriches transient details
- resolve transient peer-chat details only while those observables are actively observed
- show nested chats expanded by default and persist explicit user collapse choices
- seed restored sessions from cached chat metadata and reconcile authoritative membership without collapsing or flickering
- preserve per-chat working directories added on main

The protocol support landed in microsoft/agent-host-protocol#455.

## Validation

- npm run compile
- npm run hygiene
- affected Agent Host state/service/provider and Sessions list unit suites: 1,058 passing, 27 pending

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The complete changed call path is explicit: observed peer detail -> retained reference -> async subscription error -> deletion -> microtask reacquire -> fresh subscribe/restore. The only magnitude uncertainty is how often persistent restore failures occur, not whether they loop.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Repeated IPC subscribe requests and repeated provider/database/filesystem session-restore work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every observed failing session, each failed subscribe queues the next attempt immediately; work grows without bound with failure duration and multiplies across simultaneously visible failing sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sustained CPU, IPC, and I/O load that can saturate the agent host while the Sessions view remains open
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A subscription failure removed the failed session-state subscription; this path did not immediately recreate it in a microtask solely because peer-chat details remained observed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new error handler deletes the failed subscription and immediately calls `_ensureSessionStateSubscription` again whenever a chat-detail reference is still held.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `queueMicrotask` block at lines 5892-5896 recreates the failed subscription immediately; this retry loop did not exist before the diff.
Findings.Title: Back off failed detail subscriptions
Findings.Impact: An expanded catalog-backed peer row keeps title/status observed. If that session cannot be restored (for example a persistently unavailable provider or corrupt backing), every restore failure immediately starts another subscribe. Server-side `AgentService.subscribe` then retries `restoreSession`, including provider materialization, transcript/database reads, and possible catalog work, indefinitely.
Findings.Evidence: `AdditionalChat._withDetails` holds the new session detail reference for rendered title/status observables. On `onDidError`, line 5892 queues an unconditional retry while that reference exists. `AgentSubscriptionManager.getSubscription` creates a fresh wire subscription after an errored entry, and `AgentService.subscribe` invokes `restoreSession` whenever no snapshot exists; restore performs registry/database/provider/history work. There is no delay or retry cap in this loop.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the reference alive but retry with bounded exponential backoff (cancelled when the last reference is released), or wait for an explicit host/provider-ready event before resubscribing; do not recursively retry in the next microtask.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The renderer-to-subscription-to-restore path and one-restore-per-distinct-session cardinality are directly established. Exact duration depends on provider and transcript size, which is reflected in medium severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent IPC subscriptions, provider materializations, transcript/database reads, and related restore allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The first observed peer row for each distinct nonresident session starts one restore; default-expanded, virtualized rows therefore fan out up to the number of distinct sessions represented in the viewport, with additional bursts as the user scrolls.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Burst I/O and CPU contention in the agent host, reducing responsiveness and throughput when opening or scrolling the Sessions view
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Catalog listings did not instantiate peer-chat rows for unloaded sessions, so rendering the session list could not subscribe to and fully restore each listed session merely to display child rows.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every reactive listener attached to a peer chat's wrapped title/status details acquires a session-detail lease; the first lease immediately starts a session-state subscription, and nested sessions now start expanded.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `_withDetails` acquisition at line 840 places full session hydration on peer-row render; the same diff seeds peers from lightweight listings and expands newly nested sessions by default, making this path reachable on view open.
Findings.Title: Bound peer-row session restoration
Findings.Impact: Opening the Sessions view with several catalog-backed multi-chat sessions can concurrently restore every distinct session whose peer row is rendered. A restore crosses IPC and can materialize the provider, read the session database and full transcript, and refresh related state even though the user has not opened any chat.
Findings.Evidence: `SessionChatItemRenderer.renderElement` reactively reads both `chat.title` and `chat.status`; line 840 now turns those reads into `_acquireDetails()`. The reference collection calls `_ensureSessionStateSubscription`, which issues `connection.getSubscription`. Server-side `AgentService.subscribe` calls `restoreSession` for a missing snapshot; `_restoreSessionState` performs provider metadata/materialization, database metadata, and `_getChatMessages`. Restore coalescing is only per session key, and this new client path has no shared limiter across distinct sessions.
Findings.Recommendation: Queue row-triggered restores through a small provider-wide concurrency limiter, preserving per-session coalescing and cancellation when the row/reference disappears; alternatively keep catalog values until an explicitly prioritized interaction requests transient details.

Scenarios.Scenario: List sessions and construct catalog-backed chat facades
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The root listSessions request must complete before fresh rows are available; cached application metadata can render first on a warm start. Mapping chat summaries and constructing facades is synchronous after the listing response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and serialize the session list, now including lightweight chat metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One list request per refresh; payload grows by the effective chat count across returned sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same listSessions IPC occurred, but its payload omitted chat arrays and default-chat identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response is on the cold-list critical path, though warm cached rows can render before it completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/validate registered catalog envelopes used to produce session rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing bounded per-session catalog resolution, grouped by one listing refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same verified catalog rows were read; this diff projects already-decoded chat fields into metadata without opening each per-session transcript database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for an authoritative cold listing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize lightweight chats into the application-scoped session cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 100 cached sessions per host, with each session's catalog chat count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cached session entries omitted chat metadata and were smaller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence is not required before rows progress; deserialization is on warm-cache startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of listed sessions (application cache capped at 100 per host) and ordered non-tool chats per session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The host's existing catalog listing uses bounded limiters for per-session catalog/fallback resolution; client mapping is serial in-memory work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm startup uses the capped persisted session cache, now including lightweight chats. Cold listing reads the host catalog. Successful list results replace/update facades; no new negative cache was introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed mappings and cache cap are explicit; no new per-session database boundary is introduced by list projection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Chat counts and payload sizes vary, but the persisted session-count cap and absence of transcript data keep this bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression in listing itself; added CPU/bytes scale with lightweight catalog size and remain bounded/cached.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or scroll the Sessions view with catalog-backed peer chats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Catalog rows render immediately, but each rendered peer row's reactive title/status listener starts asynchronous session hydration. The restore is off the initial DOM paint path but competes with subsequent host work and is required before transient child status is authoritative.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to full session state when a rendered peer title or status becomes observed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active subscribe per distinct rendered session after reference coalescing, not one per chat property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unloaded listed sessions had no catalog peer rows, so list rendering did not subscribe merely to display those peers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous to initial row paint, but starts immediately and consumes host capacity while the view is used.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read registry/session metadata, cached chat data, transcript/history, and persisted state for each missing session snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full restore per distinct cold visible session, concurrent across session keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This boundary was reached when a session was explicitly opened or otherwise subscribed, not by newly listed peer-row rendering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the requested live peer details and competes with user-initiated session operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider recovery/materializeChat and related restore integration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one provider materialization per cold session in the row-triggered burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider materialization was not triggered solely by rendering an unloaded session's peer row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can dominate restore duration and consume provider resources.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct nonresident sessions represented by rendered peer rows in the viewport; multiple peer rows in one session coalesce to one subscription.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: References coalesce per session, but restores for different sessions start concurrently with no shared limiter. Default expansion makes this occur on first render; scrolling can introduce further sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A resident session snapshot avoids restore. A cold/nonresident session performs full restore. References retain subscriptions while observed and then use the existing 30-second idle-release policy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderer reads wrapped observables, the first reference calls getSubscription, and server subscribe restores missing session snapshots.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport height, number of multi-chat sessions, transcript size, and provider restore latency vary; these affect severity, not the unbounded cross-session scheduling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity concurrency burst; preserve lazy hydration but apply shared backpressure or stronger interaction prioritization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep a peer row observed while its session subscription repeatedly fails
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each failed subscription settles before the error handler queues the next attempt; retries remain active as long as any wrapped peer detail is observed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeatedly issue fresh session subscribe requests after each error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unbounded over failure duration for each observed failing session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A failed detail subscription was not immediately recreated solely because a catalog peer remained rendered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not needed for catalog row display, but continuously consumes renderer/host throughput.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeat registry, provider, database, transcript, and possible catalog restore work until failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One restore attempt per retry; unbounded sequentially per failing session and parallel across sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No microtask retry loop repeatedly re-entered restore from this observed-row path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can saturate resources needed by unrelated agent operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Failure duration and number of simultaneously observed sessions with persistent restore errors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sequential unbounded retries per session, concurrent across failing sessions. Same-key in-flight coalescing does not help because each retry starts after the prior failure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Errored subscriptions are evicted rather than negatively cached. The changed code retries in the next microtask with no backoff, retry budget, or provider-ready gate.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: error event, deletion, microtask reacquire, fresh subscription creation, and server restore are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persistent failures may be uncommon, but provider unavailability and corrupt/missing session backing are realistic; exact retry period depends on how quickly each restore fails.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity repeated-work regression; retries need cancellation-aware backoff or readiness-driven scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a session from cached ordered chat metadata and reconcile authoritative peers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The cached chat-catalog read is started after provider metadata resolution and awaited where the restore already needed cached peer data; default-chat and peer registration complete before restored state is published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached-catalog read per session restore, as before, now initiated earlier for overlap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache read occurred later immediately before default-chat working-directory restoration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before restored summary construction and peer restoration; earlier start can reduce rather than increase latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read session metadata and transcript and restore peer backings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one restore pipeline per session, with same-key coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Full restore already performed these operations; this diff additionally seeds lightweight peer summaries before enrichment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before session subscription snapshot is returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of cached chats in the restored session and provider-returned peer entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The catalog read overlaps intervening restore preparation; peer restoration retains its existing Promise.all behavior. Membership reconciliation is linear over session chats after a Set is built.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm catalog metadata seeds stable facades; provider/live data enriches them and removes stale non-tool peers. Missing cache follows existing provider restore behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the moved promise and reuse of the same awaited result are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Peer catalog sizes vary, but reconciliation uses sets/maps and is dominated by pre-existing restore boundaries.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression; the changed cache-read placement overlaps existing work and lightweight reconciliation is bounded by one session's chat catalog.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user collapse/expand event synchronously updates an in-memory Set, JSON-serializes it, and calls profile storage; list reconstruction parses it once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize all collapsed resource identifiers on each explicit collapse-state change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile-storage write per changed user toggle, containing the current collapsed set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Per-session nested collapse state was not persisted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously in the collapse event handler, but normal sets are small.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write or remove profile-scoped collapse state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write/removal per explicit changed toggle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No storage operation occurred for nested-session toggles.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct resources currently recorded as collapsed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-driven, serialized events; no background fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Expanded resources are removed and empty state deletes the storage key. Deleted sessions are not explicitly pruned, so stale identifiers can remain, but realistic retained volume was not established as large enough for a reportable impact.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for synchronous serialization/storage; lower for material magnitude of stale-key retention.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Stale keys are theoretically unbounded after deleting collapsed sessions, but no repository evidence establishes realistic cardinality sufficient for material latency or memory impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: storage work is user-frequency-bound and the evidence does not establish a material realistic degradation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files. Reported the row-triggered cross-session restore burst and the unbounded immediate retry loop after subscription failure. Checked listing/cache serialization, restore boundaries, per-session coalescing, concurrency limits, live catalog propagation, and collapse-state persistence; no other high-confidence material regression was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
